title: Experimental In Vivo Mammalian Sepsis Models
objective: In live mammalian models of experimentally induced sepsis, what therapies or care interventions improve survival, organ injury, and clinical outcomes?
question: In live mammalian models of experimentally induced sepsis, what therapies or care interventions improve survival, organ injury, and clinical outcomes?

pico.population:
In vivo mammalian models (mice, rats, pigs, sheep, rabbits, etc.)
• Approved models: Cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) and variants (cecal incision, cecum/colon ligation & dissection)
• Fecal-induced peritonitis (FIP) and colon ascendants stent peritonitis (CASP)
• Fibrin clot, agar pellet, and fecal pellet implantation models
• Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) and neonatal sepsis
• Live pathogens (E. coli, Pseudomonas, Klebsiella, Staph, Strep, Candida) paired with systemic sepsis/bacteremia
pico.intervention:
Any therapy, drug, compound, or standard supportive care used for sepsis
• All doses, routes (IV, IP, oral), and frequencies are included
• All timings included: given either before induction (pre-treatment) or after induction (rescue)
• Combination treatments co-administered with other therapies are included
pico.comparator:
All studies with or without comparisons are included
• Placebo, vehicle, sham surgery, active comparator, or no treatment
pico.outcomes:
Sepsis survival and mortality rates
• Multi-organ dysfunction (acute kidney injury, lung injury, liver failure)
• Inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β) and bacteremia clearance
• Hemodynamic and physiological parameters (MAP, lactate, microcirculation)
pico.studyDesign:
Primary empirical research studies only
• Published in English
• Publication date limit: 2020 to the present
• Excludes reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, letters, and conference abstracts

inclusionCriteria: In vivo mammalian animal model (e.g. mouse, rat, pig, sheep, rabbit).
Experimentally induced sepsis using approved models (CLP variants, FIP, CASP, fecal/agar pellet implantation, NEC, live bacterial/fungal inoculation causing sepsis).
Evaluates an intervention hypothesized to be beneficial/therapeutic for sepsis (given before or after induction).
Primary research paper published in English from 2020 to the present.

exclusionCriteria.label: Clinical Paper / Human Patients
exclusionCriteria.description: Human clinical trials, ICU patient studies, observational cohorts, or clinical case reports. Our review is strictly limited to preclinical mammalian laboratory animal models!

exclusionCriteria.label: LPS / Endotoxin Model (Excluded)
exclusionCriteria.description: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) or endotoxemia challenge models. Pure endotoxin injection is excluded from our review!

exclusionCriteria.label: In Vitro / Ex Vivo / Non-Mammalian
exclusionCriteria.description: Cell cultures, organoids, tissue slices, or non-mammalian organisms (like zebrafish, fruit flies, or worms).

exclusionCriteria.label: Wrong Disease Model
exclusionCriteria.description: Models of sterile acute lung injury (ALI), non-septic trauma, stroke, burns, or local infections that do not model systemic sepsis.

exclusionCriteria.label: Review / Abstract / Commentary
exclusionCriteria.description: Systematic reviews, narrative reviews, editorials, letters, or conference abstracts without a full peer-reviewed paper.

exclusionCriteria.label: Published Before 2020
exclusionCriteria.description: Any study published in 2019 or earlier (our search date limit is 2020 to present).

screeningTips: 🩺 Clinical vs. Preclinical: Human patient studies and clinical trials are excluded under EX-CLINICAL. Look for laboratory animal models (mice, rats, pigs, sheep)!
🚨 The #1 Trap: Watch out for LPS! Sepsis researchers love LPS injections, but our protocol strictly EXCLUDES pure LPS/endotoxin models. Look for CLP, CASP, or live bacteria instead.
📅 Glance at the publication year: If it was published before 2020, it’s an automatic EXCLUDE under EX-PRE2020.
🐭 Check the organism: Must be live whole mammals (mice, rats, pigs, etc.). If you see 'RAW 264.7 macrophages' or 'isolated splenocytes' without in vivo animal experiments, exclude it!
⏰ Timing doesn't matter: Whether the drug was given 2 hours before CLP (pretreatment) or 6 hours after (rescue therapy), both are INCLUDED.

🛡️ The Golden Rule: When in doubt between CLP and LPS or if the abstract is vague, lean towards INCLUDE or MAYBE. You can always check the full-text methods, but a wrongly excluded study is gone forever!
